newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil prison siege ends, hostages freed.
newsitem.headline: Brazil prison siege ends, hostages freed.

text.p: Inmates at a Brazilian prison ended a tense 24-hour standoff on Monday, freeing unharmed five guards they were holding hostage.
Officials said prisoners and authorities struck a deal to end the siege that began on Sunday at the prison in Sao Vicente, on the Atlantic coast 19 miles (30 kms) south of Santos port.
"It's all over and, thank God, nobody was hurt," one prison official, who requested anonymity, told Reuters.
According to news reports, authorities agreed to some of the inmates' demands, including a probe of alleged beatings by prison guards and improved living conditions.
When the hostages were released, the last of almost 450 visitors caught inside when the riot broke out during visiting hours on Sunday afternoon also left the prison.
Relatives who had spent the night inside the prison said the 70 visiting men had stayed behind with the prisoners out of fear the police would attack the inmates.
"They're afraid shock troops will move in and beat the prisoners," said Silvana da Silva, whose husband was among the prisoners.
Prison riots are a regular occurance in Brazil, where conditions are poor in notoriously overcrowded jails.
